title: Online Learning: A Modern Introduction Using Convex Optimization
author: Francesco Orabona

sourceOnlySlots.content: Finite horizon T with entries a_0,...,a_T >= 0. The offset a_0 is among these entries. The text states no strict positivity or lower bound on T.
f is non-increasing on its domain. Equality is permitted.
f is continuous on the stated domain, including its finite endpoint.
For round t=1,...,T the weight is a_t and the sample point is the current right endpoint a_0 + sum_{i=1}^t a_i. The proof writes this endpoint as s_t = sum_{i=0}^t a_i.
Integrate f(x) dx from a_0 to sum_{t=0}^T a_t. Both integration limits depend on the supplied data; s_0 = a_0 and s_T = sum_{t=0}^T a_t.
sum_{t=1}^T a_t f(a_0 + sum_{i=1}^t a_i) <= integral_{a_0}^{sum_{t=0}^T a_t} f(x) dx. This is an exact finite, one-sided inequality with coefficient 1.

correspondence: Offset separate. Source increments 1 through T correspond to Lean indices 0 through T-1. The total real extension is constrained on Ici 0. The value of f on negative inputs is irrelevant. Source nonnegativity of f remains in the signature although the local proof does not use it.
